org.name: Cal.com
org.one_liner: A fully customizable scheduling software for individuals, businesses taking calls and developers building scheduling platforms where users meet users.

facts.claim: Cal.diy is the open source community edition and a fork of Cal.com with all enterprise/commercial code removed.
Cal.diy is strictly recommended for personal, non-production use by self-hosters.
For commercial and enterprise-ready scheduling infrastructure, Cal.com must be used instead of Cal.diy.
Cal.diy is 100% MIT-licensed with no proprietary 'Enterprise Edition' features and no 'Open Core' split.
Enterprise features like Teams, Organizations, Insights, Workflows, and SSO/SAML have been removed from Cal.diy.
Cal.diy requires no license key, no Cal.com account, and no Cal.com license to work.
Cal.diy is a self-hosted project with no hosted or managed version available.
Cal.diy is built using Next.js, tRPC, React.js, Tailwind CSS, Prisma.io, and Daily.co.
Prerequisites for running Cal.diy are Node.js (>=18.x), PostgreSQL (>=13.x), and Yarn.
Default test credentials are seeded for free, pro, trial, admin, and onboarding users.
Cal.com is a fully customizable scheduling software for individuals, businesses taking calls, and developers building scheduling platforms.
Cal.com is unlimited and free for individuals.
Cal Video is Cal.com's in-house video conferencing platform.
Cal.com supports over 65 languages for global booking capabilities.
Users can monetize bookings directly through a Stripe integration.
The Cal.com API features three authentication methods: OAuth, API key, and Platform (which is deprecated).
The default rate limit for Cal.com API keys is 120 requests per minute.
As of December 15, 2025, Cal.com is restructuring its 'Platform' offering and no longer accepts new signups for Platform plans, though existing enterprise customers continue to receive support.
Under Cal.com's Platform managed user authentication, access tokens are valid for 60 minutes and refresh tokens are valid for 1 year.
